purpose: Broad, literature-driven candidate expansion around institutional holdings, filing text, risk networks, insider information and beneficial ownership.

external_basis.observation: Quarterly as-filed XML-derived data sets are publicly available from July 2013 through August 2026.

external_basis.source: Which investors drive anomaly returns and how? (JFE 2026)
external_basis.observation: The paper finds anomaly variation is linked to heterogeneous investor trading motives and distinguishes fundamental-based from institution-led channels.

external_basis.source: Risk-based peer networks and return predictability (Journal of Empirical Finance 2026)
external_basis.observation: 10-K risk disclosures are used to form text-based peer networks with reported cross-firm lead-lag predictability.

external_basis.source: Uncertain Text and Price Reactions to Earnings Releases (JBF 2026)
external_basis.observation: 10-K/Q textual uncertainty is reported to interact with immediate earnings-surprise reactions, post-earnings drift and institutional attention.

external_basis.source: Insider trading, future earnings, and PEAD
external_basis.observation: Prior literature links insider trading around earnings to the magnitude of post-earnings announcement drift.

candidates.name: N-PORT Position Change × Accrual State
candidates.hypothesis: Changes in publicly reported monthly fund positions may have different implications when the issuer is simultaneously in a fixed accrual state.
candidates.construction: PIT N-PORT reported position change for mapped securities × latest eligible SEC XBRL accrual state; freeze by EDGAR acceptance timestamps; no weighting search.
pit_requirements: position-as-of date vs public filing date
candidates.next_gate: N-PORT archive coverage + security mapping + PIT publication-lag audit

candidates.name: N-PORT Concentration Shock × Filing Uncertainty
candidates.hypothesis: A change in fund concentration toward an issuer may interact with the uncertainty/fuzziness of the issuer's newest public filing.
candidates.construction: Deterministic concentration-change state from frozen N-PORT holdings × frozen filing-text uncertainty metric on the latest eligible 10-K/Q; both anchored to public availability.
candidates.next_gate: N-PORT history + SEC text archive + immutable text fingerprinting

candidates.name: Risk-Network Peer Shock × Focal Filing Arrival
candidates.hypothesis: When a risk-similar peer files before the focal issuer, the peer's recent price move may contain information about a delayed focal response.
candidates.construction: Deterministic similarity graph from fixed-window 10-K risk text; edge set frozen only from filings public by cutoff; focal state uses prior peer return and peer filing-arrival status.
pit_requirements: no graph recomputation with future filings
candidates.next_gate: text archive depth + graph PIT mutation tests

candidates.name: Disclosure Uncertainty × Institutional Attention
candidates.hypothesis: The market response to a new filing may depend on whether institutional portfolios subsequently exhibit a detectable public holdings change.
candidates.construction: Fixed textual uncertainty state × next-public N-PORT holdings-change state, with no outcome-conditioned matching and no free-form LLM scoring.
candidates.next_gate: N-PORT historical feasibility + text metric deterministic benchmark

candidates.name: Insider Trade × Earnings Drift State
candidates.hypothesis: The direction and intensity of PIT-verified insider transactions may modify the persistence of a subsequent earnings-surprise reaction.
candidates.construction: Fixed Form 4 transaction-direction state anchored to EDGAR acceptance time × fixed earnings-event state; no transaction filtering after observing returns.
candidates.next_gate: Form 4 archive coverage + transaction-code integrity + event-time mapping

candidates.name: Beneficial Ownership Transition × Filing Event
candidates.hypothesis: New 13D/13G ownership-state transitions may carry a different short-horizon response when they coincide with a fresh issuer filing event.
candidates.construction: Deterministic ownership-transition state from 13D/13G/13D-A/13G-A filings × focal issuer filing-arrival state; use EDGAR acceptance time as the public-availability anchor.

candidates.name: Common-Holder Network Connectedness × Filing Arrival
candidates.hypothesis: The structure of common institutional ownership may alter how quickly public issuer disclosures are incorporated into prices: firms embedded in more connected institutional-holder networks may exhibit a different short-horizon response to newly public filings.
candidates.construction: Build a deterministic quarterly manager-security bipartite graph from PIT-valid Form 13F holdings; derive an issuer-level network-connectedness exposure from disclosed common ownership, then combine that frozen exposure with the focal issuer's newly public filing-arrival state using only information available at the filing acceptance cutoff.
pit_requirements: quarter-end holdings versus public filing date separation
candidates.next_gate: 13F graph construction integrity + PIT publication-lag mutation tests
literature_basis: Information sharing within institutional investor networks (Journal of Accounting & Economics, 2026), DOI 10.1016/j.jacceco.2025.101803

notes: Q109 is an expansion inventory, not evidence.
No candidate is ranked, scored, selected or performance-authorized.
Text features must be deterministic and frozen before any performance use; free-form LLM scoring is not authorized.
N-PORT is treated as a separate institutional channel from 13F rather than silently pooling the two.
Any historical publication lag or archive limitation becomes a hard feasibility boundary.
Q109:N7 was added as a design-only 13F common-holder network hypothesis inspired by a 2026 institutional-investor-network study; it remains unranked and performance-ineligible.
